set.reason: The target explicitly transforms equations, requiring their equality/unknown meaning. Gemini correctly observes that solution-testing is not needed, but the necessary endpoint component is equation meaning, not every verification criterion.
set.scope: Equation and unknown meaning when using equality properties to transform an equation

set.reason: Substitution introduces the reduction-to-one-variable idea, but adding equations to cancel an unknown is justified independently by equality operations.
A constant difference is imposed on consecutive terms of a sequence, so terms and their order supply the objects in the definition.
The arithmetic general-term formula uses the initial term and common difference defined by an arithmetic sequence.
The general term gives a useful three-term model, while equal adjacent differences directly yield 2b=a+c. No nth-term formula is necessary.

Fraction division prepares ratio values with fractional terms. The target expressly permits a simple ratio, and a whole-number pair such as 6 to 3 needs only ordinary division; no fraction-by-fraction division is universal.
